title: Pembrolizumab + axitinib
context_label: Advanced clear-cell-component kidney cancer · first line
indication_text: First-line advanced renal cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component, with or without sarcomatoid features, meeting current NCCP prior-treatment criteria.
purpose: Help control advanced kidney cancer using immunotherapy and a blood-vessel-growth inhibitor.
schedule_label: Pembrolizumab every 21 days · axitinib twice daily
schedule_summary: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given intravenously every 21 days. Axitinib starts at 5 mg twice daily, about 12 hours apart, continuously, with or without food. Only your team may change the dose. Do not take an extra axitinib dose after a missed or vomited dose. Duration depends on benefit, tolerance and the agreed plan.
administration_text: Pembrolizumab runs over 30 minutes with observation according to local policy. Swallow axitinib tablets whole with water; follow the prescribed twice-daily dose and pharmacy instructions.
monitoring_summary: Review blood pressure, blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose and thyroid function regularly. The team specifies dates and any home blood-pressure record. ECG, cortisol and other tests are added when indicated. Review diarrhoea, breathing, rash, fatigue and endocrine symptoms before each infusion.
safety_note: Follow your own prescription and hospital instructions. This information supports a discussion; it does not authorise treatment.
urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999.

agents.name: Pembrolizumab
agents.explanation: Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can limit the activity of immune cells. This can help them attack cancer, but can also cause inflammation in healthy organs during treatment or after it ends.
agents.watch: Report new diarrhoea, cough, breathlessness, rash, headache, unusual weakness, thirst or changes in urine promptly.
risks: Immune inflammation can affect the lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, skin, eyes, heart, muscles or nervous system and can be severe or fatal
Hormone-gland inflammation can affect the thyroid, pituitary or adrenal glands; diabetes can occur and hormone replacement may be lifelong
Severe skin reactions, including blistering or peeling; infusion reactions
Immune effects can start during treatment or months after stopping; tell every healthcare professional about immunotherapy

agents.name: Axitinib
agents.type: Targeted therapy: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.mechanism: Axitinib blocks vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFRs), signals that help tumours grow new blood vessels. Reducing this blood supply can slow cancer growth. The same action explains effects on blood pressure, kidneys, bleeding and wound healing.
agents.explanation: Axitinib blocks vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFRs), signals that help tumours grow new blood vessels. Reducing this blood supply can slow cancer growth. The same action explains effects on blood pressure, kidneys, bleeding and wound healing.
risks: High blood pressure, sometimes severe; rare heart failure, heart attack, stroke or clots
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, constipation, reduced appetite and weight loss
Sore mouth, taste changes, fatigue and voice changes
Painful, red or peeling palms and soles; rash and dry skin
Thyroid changes, liver-test abnormalities and protein in the urine
Bleeding, occasionally serious; rare bowel perforation or abnormal connections (fistulas)
Delayed wound healing; rare reversible brain swelling syndrome (PRES)
Anaemia and changes in other blood cells; possible fertility and pregnancy harm
agents.watch: Collect a prescription for diarrhoea medicine, usually loperamide, before starting. Follow the supplied instructions and contact the team for persistent diarrhoea, dizziness, poor intake or reduced urine.

anatomy: New cough or breathlessness may mean immune inflammation; call urgently.
Report severe tiredness, dizziness, headache, thirst or frequent urination.
Monitor blood pressure; chest pain, collapse or stroke symptoms need emergency help.
Report diarrhoea early; blood, severe pain or persistent diarrhoea needs urgent review.
Tests monitor the liver; report yellow eyes, dark urine or severe nausea.
Report reduced urine, swelling or blood in urine; protein may need testing.
Report painful palms/soles, widespread rash, blistering or peeling.
Severe headache, confusion, seizures, weakness or vision change needs emergency help.

evidence.title: KEYNOTE-426 · first interim report, 2019
evidence.summary: KEYNOTE-426 randomised 861 people to pembrolizumab/axitinib or sunitinib. In the first interim analysis, 12-month overall survival was 89.9% versus 78.3%; median progression-free survival was 15.1 versus 11.1 months.
evidence.intro: KEYNOTE-426 randomised 861 people to pembrolizumab/axitinib or sunitinib. In the first interim analysis, 12-month overall survival was 89.9% versus 78.3%; median progression-free survival was 15.1 versus 11.1 months.
evidence.caveat: These are the dated initial trial results, not a personalised prognosis or the latest follow-up. The trial compared with sunitinib, not every current first-line combination. Its treatment-duration rules do not automatically define the NCCP prescription.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.
